archetype.name: Overachiever (still short of October)
archetype.definition: An 86-win team whose run differential of about +9 pointed closer to 82 wins, held up by an A- bullpen, good defense and an elite catcher, and it still finished third in the division and out of the postseason.

report.headline: A great bullpen and Moreno kept a D- rotation afloat, but not into October

recap.finish: 86-76, third in the NL West (5 games behind SD, 14 behind LAD); missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a middle-of-the-pack team that played a little above its station. Arizona finished 11th in runs per game and 17th in runs allowed, and outscored opponents by only 0.06 runs a game. That is about nine runs over the full season, the profile of a .500-ish club. The 86-76 record came from a W vs Run Diff of +4.1, sixth-most in the league. That is close-game fortune more than a repeatable skill, and the franchise ran the same +4.5 in 2023.

The months show it. April went 14-11 even though the Diamondbacks were outscored 117-138. May was the best-pitched month (91 allowed in 28 games) but returned only 15-13. June was the real dip: 12-15 and outscored by 32. July (15-10, +27) was the strongest stretch, and August and September were roughly even. The streaks never got long, six wins at most and four losses at most. The longest win streak came late in September: a series win over the Yankees, a sweep at Colorado and an 11-4 opener in San Diego. Then the Padres took the final two, the last series against a team that finished five games ahead of them.

The club was strong up the middle. Gabriel Moreno was the No. 1 catcher on the site, with a 141 wRC+ and a .388 OBP worth 5.4 WAR. Geraldo Perdomo added 5.0 WAR from shortstop with a .370 OBP and 11 Def Runs. Corbin Carroll (4.2 WAR, 115 wRC+) and Nolan Arenado (30 HR, 120 wRC+) gave the lineup its power. The B- hitter grade was dragged down at the corners: first base went to Ildemaro Vargas (84 wRC+) and Tim Tawa (89), and DH Jesús Sánchez finished at -0.4 WAR. In a 106 park, a .720 team OPS ranked only 11th, a clear step down from the 2024 and 2025 offenses (.777 and .758).

The staff split sharply in two. The bullpen graded A-. Juan Morillo posted a 2.24 ERA with 19 holds, and Jonathan Loáisiga a 2.42, both backed by FIPs under 2.90. Only Dennis Santana (5.56) was a weak spot among the main relievers. The rotation graded D-. Merrill Kelly and Zack Littell combined for about 286 innings at below replacement level (-1.0 WAR). Littell's 6.08 FIP was the ugliest number on the staff. Eduardo Rodriguez's 2.89 ERA made him an All-Star, but his 3.89 FIP says the results ran ahead of the pitching. A 4.18 team ERA ranked 18th, though run prevention (17th) was the franchise's best since at least 2021, helped by 22.8 Fielding Runs.

The result was a six-win improvement on 2025's 80-82, without a real change in what the team was. The margin says it was closer to a .500 club than the record shows. It was good enough to beat the bottom of the division and not good enough to catch San Diego.

highlights.title: A bullpen that held everything together
highlights.body: The relief corps earned an A- grade, built on Juan Morillo and Jonathan Loáisiga, whose FIPs back up their ERAs. Their strikeout and walk rates suggest the core is real rather than a sequencing fluke. Taylor Clarke's 2.96 ERA over a 3.85 FIP is the one to expect to slip.

highlights.title: Moreno and Perdomo up the middle
highlights.body: The best catcher on the site and a 5-WAR shortstop gave Arizona more than 10 wins from two premium positions. Moreno's .311/.388/.486 line was the lineup's engine. Perdomo's value came from on-base skill and glove work rather than power, which tends to hold up.

highlights.title: Defense quietly saved runs
highlights.body: Arizona ranked sixth in Fielding Runs, led by Perdomo's 11 Def Runs. That helped a mediocre staff play to the best run-prevention rank the club has posted in this five-plus-year window. Fielding has been a positive every year since 2022, so this looks like a stable trait.

lowlights.title: Two rotation spots sank the staff
lowlights.body: Kelly and Littell took about 286 innings, and both finished below replacement. Their FIPs (5.32 and 6.08) say the problem was the pitching itself, not bad luck. Strikeout rates of 16.1% and 13.5% leave little margin in a hitter-friendly park, and that is the main reason the rotation graded D-.

lowlights.title: A record ahead of the margin
lowlights.body: A +0.06 run differential per game supports roughly an 82-win team. The extra four wins came from close games, and that kind of edge rarely carries over. April's 14-11 while being outscored by 21 was the clearest example.

lowlights.title: No bat at first base or DH
lowlights.body: Arizona's first basemen and designated hitter were all below a 100 wRC+ in heavy playing time, and Sánchez finished below replacement. Those lineup spots usually supply offense. Their absence is a big part of why the scoring rank fell to 11th from the top-six levels of the previous two years.

arc.note: No month was worse than 12-15 and no streak longer than six games, though the underlying run differential swung from -32 in June to +27 in July. A six-game run in late September ended with two losses at San Diego.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is real. Moreno, Perdomo, Carroll and Arenado provided most of the position-player value, and the A- bullpen's best arms have peripherals that match their results. Fielding has been a plus every season since 2022. What doesn't carry over is the +4.1 W vs Run Diff: the same run margin would likely mean low-80s wins. The rotation also needs more than one dependable arm. Rodriguez's 2.89 ERA sits a full run below his FIP. Soroka (3.19 FIP, 24.1% strikeouts) and Pfaadt (3.89 FIP) were the steadier starters underneath. The Kelly and Littell innings are the clearest place to improve. First base and DH are the lineup's obvious gap, and filling them is the most direct way to restore the offense of 2024-25.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the luck read rests on a clear W vs Run Diff signal.
